thread: anna-docs: starting a small docs PR to cover split-horizon DNS and resolver strategies for private/VPC/on-prem installs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2028 rick-netops: great, we need a concrete section for sealed sites where customers can't run a local DNS server. include fallback options: /etc/hosts, systemd-resolved stub files, and dnsmasq on a jumpbox. short examples please. priya-engr: also add a clear note about mTLS certs being CN/SAN-bound to hostnames — if you override with IPs in /etc/hosts folks will hit TLS name mismatch. recommend adding SANs for IPs only as last resort. anna-docs: will do. planning sections: 1) VPC resolver/Route53 inbound rules (AWS example), 2) kube stubDomains/CoreDNS config for cluster-local service discovery, 3) host-file fallback patterns for sealed sites, 4) SDK examples showing how to use a custom net.Resolver for unix/local stub, 5) troubleshooting table. rick-netops: for AWS Route53 Resolver, include this Terraform snippet we usually share with customers to forward to their on-prem resolver: ```hcl resource "aws_route53_resolver_endpoint" "out" { name = "redwood-forwarder" direction = "OUTBOUND" security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.sg.id] vpc_id = aws_vpc.prod.id ip_address { subnet_id = aws_subnet.subnet1.id } } ``` Make sure to caution about source/dest check and SG egress for port 53 UDP/TCP. priya-engr: for Kubernetes add the CoreDNS stubDomain example: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: coredns namespace: kube-system data: Corefile: | .:53 { errors health hosts /etc/redwood/hosts { fallthrough } kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa forward . 8.8.8.8 cache 30 } ``` But we'll show a stubDomain snippet for examples/ too. anna-docs: adding both and a short caution: prefer DNS-based overrides over /etc/hosts for scale, but hosts file is the only option for fully air-gapped nodes without a stub resolver. rick-netops: include a systemd-resolved snippet for Ubuntu 22.04 sealed-site setups: ```ini # /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/redwood.conf [Resolve] DNS=10.10.0.10 Domains=~redwood.private FallbackDNS=1.1.1.1 ``` And note to `systemctl restart systemd-resolved`. priya-engr: SDK example would be really helpful. show a Go custom resolver that dials 127.0.0.1:5353 (local stub) so client libraries in private installs can opt-in: ```go // custom resolver that uses a local stub at 127.0.0.1:5353 r := &net.Resolver{ PreferGo: true, Dial: func(ctx context.Context, network, address string) (net.Conn, error) { d := net.Dialer{} return d.DialContext(ctx, "udp", "127.0.0.1:5353") }, } // use r.LookupHost(ctx, "hsm.redwood.private") ``` Add equivalent Python snippet using `dnspython` later. anna-docs: good — I'll add Python and a curl `--resolve` example for quick debugging: `curl --resolve hsm.redwood.private:8443:10.2.0.5 https://hsm.redwood.private:8443/health` (handy during preflight). rick-netops: we should call out SRV records for service discovery too — some customers use `_hsm._tcp.redwood.private` for port mapping. include an example `dig SRV _hsm._tcp.redwood.private` and fallback client logic. priya-engr: add a short checklist for certs: list fully-qualified names, list SANs you should include, and recommendation to pin certs to hostnames not IPs unless absolutely required. also mention automating cert reissuance when you change hostnames as part of migration guides. link-bot: CI / docs
